topic_ko: 파티 자랑에서 시작한 랩 가사가 The Message를 계기로 사회 비판으로, 다시 '존경'의 태도로 확장된 과정

passage: In its earliest days, rap was little more than shouting used to keep a party alive.
The words praised the skill of the DJ or the rapper and invited everyone to enjoy the night.
During the 1980s, however, the content of those words changed in a decisive way.
In 1982 a group called Grandmaster Flash and Furious Five released a song that described the cruelty of ghetto life in detail.
From that point on, rappers used their verses to attack unfairness rather than simply to entertain.
Later a second change appeared, one best captured by the single word respect.
Rappers honored the founders who had built a culture out of almost nothing.
They also claimed that same dignity for themselves and for the listeners who had survived alongside them.
choices: how the content of rap lyrics moved from boasting to social criticism and respect
the technical training that turns an ordinary teenager into a skilled DJ
the commercial strategies that made rap records sell in the 1980s
the daily hardships faced by children growing up in American ghettos
the influence of dance rhythms on the popularity of party music
theme.explanation_ko: 파티 자랑 → 사회 비판 → 존경이라는 가사 내용의 변화를 시간 순으로 따라가는 글이므로 ①이 주제이다.
theme.distractor_ko: ② DJ 기술 훈련은 실력 자랑이라는 도입 소재를 오해한 것이다. ③ 상업적 판매 전략은 언급이 없다. ④ 빈민가의 고난은 The Message 가사를 설명하는 예시일 뿐이다. ⑤ 리듬은 메시지를 전달하는 통로로만 나온다.

passage: Rap began as party talk, focused on fun and on showing off the DJ's or the rapper's ability.
That focus shifted sharply once hip-hop grew popular in the 1980s.

Its rhythm still moved bodies, so listeners took in the message while they danced.

Rappers honored the pioneers and, through them, honored their own worth as well.

gist.distractor_ko: ② 상업적 성공은 다루지 않는다. ③ 정책적 해결책은 언급이 없다. ④ 감정 배제는 본문과 무관하다. ⑤ 본문은 리듬과 메시지가 함께 갔다고 말하므로 정반대이다.
